subject: Post-call recap: RetailCo model fit & regression concern
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elena Torres <elena@retailco.com>, Samir Patel <samir.patel@retailco.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwoodinference.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwoodinference.com>, David Kim <david_kim@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-04-02T10:15:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call recap: RetailCo model fit & regression concern

Thanks again for taking the call this morning — great to meet the team. Quick recap and next steps from our side:

- Goals: improve product categorization precision on short title length (0-6 tokens) and reduce systematic mislabeling of accessory SKUs.
- What we observed: your team reported a drop in precision after the model v2.3 rollout last week. You flagged increased false positives on the Accessories category.
- Our recommendation (initial): pin production to v2.2 (the variant we used in the PoC) while we investigate v2.3 diffs. v2.2 shows +6.2% precision lift on your benchmark sample.

Deliverables I will share by EOD:
- Full benchmark CSV comparing v2.2 vs v2.3 on your sample (retailco_eval_v2.2_vs_v2.3.csv).
- Short diff summary PDF (model_diff_v2.2_v2.3.pdf) with examples showing where the logits shifted.
- Prompt set we ran (20 representative prompts) and the evaluation rubric.

As discussed, next steps from RetailCo: confirm if you want us to schedule a pinned rollback window (we can do a reversible pin in ~2 hours with canary validation), and confirm any procurement or security approvers we should loop in.

Proposed times for a quick 30-min rollback/check call: today 3–5pm PT or tomorrow 9–11am PT. Let me know what works.

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
marissa@redwoodinference.com

From: Elena Torres <elena@retailco.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Samir Patel <samir.patel@retailco.com>, procurement@retailco.com
Date: 2027-04-02T13:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: RetailCo model fit & regression concern

Thanks Marissa — appreciate the quick follow-up and the proposed plan. A couple of clarifications from our side:

- Impact: The drop is most visible on our weekend promotions feed (small titles). Precision for Accessories fell from 84% to 71% after v2.3. That increase in false positives triggered manual review throttles and is causing conversion impact.
- Timeline: We need the model stabilized before next Monday (2027-04-05) — unfortunately that’s a hard requirement from ops.

Can you confirm: if you pin back to v2.2, will that restore the previous behavior for all regions, or do we need to run a regional rollback? Also please include any estimated cost/time tradeoffs for keeping v2.2 pinned longer term.

Looping procurement to flag potential clause for temporary rollback support.

—Elena
VP Product, RetailCo
elena@retailco.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elena Torres <elena@retailco.com>, Samir Patel <samir.patel@retailco.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwoodinference.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwoodinference.com>, David Kim <david_kim@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-04-02T16:00:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: RetailCo model fit & regression concern

Elena — thanks for the detail. Quick answers and what we attached:

1) Will pinning v2.2 restore previous behavior?
Short answer: yes for inference behavior across all regions. v2.2 is a build that differs in final layer calibration and a tokenizer tweak introduced in v2.3; pinning routes production traffic to the v2.2 binary and will revert outputs to the prior distribution. We recommend a global pin to avoid region mismatch.

2) Cost/time tradeoffs:
- Pinning itself is configuration-level and free. If you ask us to host a dedicated pinned instance for longer-term stability, that could incur reserved capacity pricing (we'll estimate once you signal intent).
- Short rollback window (2 hours) to validate canary results: our ops can complete in ~60–90 minutes with your confirmation.

3) What we attached / links:
- retailco_eval_v2.2_vs_v2.3.csv — per-example labels and scores (see summary: overall precision delta -6.2% for Accessories).
- model_diff_v2.2_v2.3.pdf — short diff with 15 illustrative examples (token-level attention differences).
- Prompt set link: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1a2b3c (20 sample prompts we used).
- HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/1234567

4) Proposed immediate plan:
- If you approve, we will schedule a global pin to v2.2 tonight at 7pm PT. Ops will run canary validation (50k tokens) for 30 minutes. If canary passes, we will broaden the pin. If we see failures, we will re-open traffic and start a deeper investigation.
- We will preserve all request/response logs and evaluation artifacts and share a short RCA within 48 hours.

Please reply with a simple: APPROVE-ROLLBACK or REQUEST-MORE-INFO and preferred rollback window. If you want a separate SOW for longer-term pinned instances, procurement can email procurement@redwoodinference.com and Priyom will follow up.

Thanks —
Marissa

Date: 2027-04-03T09:05:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: data retention + evidence for RetailCo regression

Folks — internal note (do not forward to RetailCo):

- Make sure we snapshot the full request/response stream for the Canary run and label it RC-2026-0412-regression. This is important for the RCA and for SOC 2 evidence.
- Keep eval artifacts (CSV + diff PDF) in the internal retention bucket for 90 days and create a short Jira (INF-4792) linking the artifacts and the HubSpot deal ID.
- If we make a config-level pin, capture the rollout plan in the change log and annotate the deployment tag.

Rishi/Priyom — please coordinate ops timeline today and confirm we have a rollback playbook ready.

Thanks,
David
Director, Security & Compliance
